faulerhund1215: Jakub Faulerhund joined the replacements on Day 5. An old hand checked his pack straps before asking his name.
The section held a competition for the worst joke. Jakub Faulerhund won before reaching the end of his entry.
hohlmike4: Isidor Hohlmike stepped off the supply cart at R-F3 and stood very still, listening to the guns as if they were saying his name.
An unexploded shell lay beside the approach trench. Isidor Hohlmike helped steer the carrying party around it and was glad to leave the problem to somebody else.
Isidor Hohlmike dreamt about missing a train. Waking up here felt like a harsh punishment for it.
j_ak_u_b1: On the way to S-S9, Felix Jakub tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.
Felix Jakub remembered the tune but not the words. Six men offered six different songs, and none of them helped.
kirov_34: On Day 5, Oskar Kirov arrived during an argument about a missing spoon. The war already had matters more urgent than introductions.

Oskar Kirov tried to write home with gloves on. The address is readable. Everything else will need some imagination. Mail came up the line with a letter for Oskar Kirov. Oskar Kirov read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
